subject.title: fix(agents): exclude MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap

question: Should OpenClaw enforce the documented rule that root MEMORY.md never auto-loads in any shared group or channel session, accepting the upgrade change for users who relied on the undocumented behavior?
rationale: The patch is technically sound and fixes a demonstrated disclosure path, but this security default intentionally changes established runtime behavior across every channel and therefore needs an owner to accept the compatibility consequence.

options.title: Enforce the boundary
options.body: Adopt this channel-agnostic private-memory rule, rebase the branch, and land it after the current checks complete.

options.title: Add an unsafe compatibility opt-in
options.body: Preserve an explicit operator-controlled escape hatch, at the cost of new configuration surface and continued disclosure risk when enabled.

options.title: Pause the cross-channel change
options.body: Hold the PR for a different ownership design, leaving the currently demonstrated shared-session exposure unresolved meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Enforce the boundary
recommendation.body: Adopt this channel-agnostic private-memory rule, rebase the branch, and land it after the current checks complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans both root-memory policy and central session routing, which are the two owner boundaries involved in this decision.
